guangdong.population: annual incidence rate ~50 per 100,000 (highly seasonal, May-November peak)

clinical_features: High fever (39-40°C) with sudden onset ('breakbone fever')
Maculopapular rash (days 3-5, 'islands of white in a sea of red')
diagnosis.gold_standard: RT-PCR (acute phase) or paired serology (IgM seroconversion)

treatment.indication: All dengue patients — maintain adequate urine output
Warning signs present or severe dengue with plasma leakage
Platelets <20,000/μL with active bleeding OR <50,000/μL with major bleeding

risk_factors: Living in or traveling to endemic southern China provinces
Urban/peri-urban areas with Aedes mosquito breeding sites
Prior dengue infection (different serotype → increased severe dengue risk — antibody-dependent enhancement)
prevention: Aedes mosquito control: eliminate standing water (flower pots, tires, containers)
Long-sleeved clothing during peak mosquito activity (early morning, late afternoon)
Dengue vaccine (CYD-TDV / Dengvaxia) — ONLY in seropositive individuals (prior dengue infection confirmed) due to risk of severe dengue in seronegative vaccinees

clinical_examples.description: A 32-year-old woman from Guangzhou presents in August with 3 days of high fever (39.5°C), severe headache, muscle pain, and a new petechial rash on her arms and legs. CBC: WBC 2.3×10^9/L, platelets 78×10^9/L, Hct 42% (baseline 37%). NS1 antigen: positive. Liver enzymes: AST 180 U/L, ALT 150 U/L.
clinical_examples.key_findings: Fever + retro-orbital headache + myalgia + petechiae + thrombocytopenia + leukopenia + NS1+ → dengue fever with warning signs (thrombocytopenia, elevated AST)
clinical_examples.outcome: Admitted for close monitoring. IVF hydration at maintenance rate. Daily CBC monitoring. Platelets nadir at 35×10^9/L on day 5. No bleeding. Hct peaked at 44% (mild hemoconcentration). Discharged day 7 with platelets recovering to 95×10^9/L. Advised to avoid NSAIDs/aspirin.
